newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek minister slams EU's "racism" towards Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Greek minister slams EU's "racism" towards Turkey.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos slammed Europe's reluctance to embrace Turkey because of its Moslem identity on Tuesday, saying it was tantamount to fascism.
Setting aside differences that brought the Aegean neighbours to the brink of war last year, the outspoken minister told a Balkan economic conference that Turkey's place was in Europe.
"Greece considers unacceptable the view that Turkey lacks the cultural characteristics to be in Europe," he said. "This is a tactic that we reject and we will fight."

European Union officials recently voiced concerns within the 15-member bloc about letting in a large Moslem nation. Turkey, which has a customs union agreement with the EU, has seen its bid to join the EU put off repeatedly.
Greece, which has long blocked closer relations between the EU and its eastern neighbour, rushed to Turkey's defence after the Moslem issue came out.
Pangalos said that excluding one religion from the European family could soon lead to racism and discrimination on the basis of religion and political views.
"That's how fascism started everywhere and it finally destroyed Europe. It started by rejecting the Jews, then the communists and then everyone who thought like them," he said.

Pangalos sang the praises of Islam to scores of Balkan ministers, officials and businessmen at the two-day conference, saying history proved that Europe progressed when in contact with Moslem nations and sunk into the Dark Ages when isolated.
But the minister also seized the opportunity to attack perceived Turkish aggression against Greece and to ask Turkey to take its disputes to the International Court of Justice at the Hague.
The two NATO members have long been at odds over rights in the Aegean, the divided island of Cyprus and minority rights in both countries.
"(The Hague) is a dignified and just procedure," Pangalos said, rejecting a long-standing Turkish proposal for direct dialogue.
He said Turkey must stop boasting about its military might, large population and readiness to launch war on Greece if it wants to seek a European future.

Already tense Greek-Turkish relations have been further strained since January 1996, when their warships nearly clashed over a deserted islet in the eastern Aegean. War was averted with last minute intervention by the United States.
